title: The Git Quest
body:
Goal: make your first save points (commits) with git, look back in time, spot a change, and undo a mistake.

You will track one small art program, hero_badge.py (it is in this folder), inside a brand-new folder called git-quest. Everything stays on your Mac: no website, no account.

Type each command in Terminal exactly, then press Return. Lines starting with # are notes for you - do not type them.

Before you start (once per Mac, done by your teacher)

git --version

If you see something like git version 2.39.5, git is ready. If a window pops up asking to install "command line developer tools", your teacher clicks Install (free, no Apple ID needed) and waits.

Level 1 - Make a quest folder

cd ~/Documents
mkdir git-quest
cd git-quest

Now copy hero_badge.py into the git-quest folder (drag it in Finder, or use File > Save As... in Thonny and pick Documents/git-quest).

ls

You should see hero_badge.py.

Level 2 - Tell git who you are (a nickname, not your real name)

git config --global user.name "PixelFox"
git config --global user.email "pixelfox@example.com"

Use YOUR nickname. example.com is a pretend address that is safe to use. Your real name and real email never go into the history.

Level 3 - Start the save system

git init
git status

git status says hero_badge.py is untracked: git sees it but is not saving it yet.

Level 4 - Your first save point

git add hero_badge.py
git commit -m "Add hero badge drawing"
git log --oneline

The log shows one line: a short code (the commit id) and your message.

Level 5 - Change something and spot the difference

  1. Open hero_badge.py in Thonny (from the git-quest folder).
  2. Change BADGE_COLOR to another color from the palette, e.g. "#009E73".
  3. Change HERO_NAME to your own made-up hero name. Save. Run it to see it.
git diff

Lines with - were removed, lines with + were added. Now save it:

git add hero_badge.py
git commit -m "Change badge color to green"
git log --oneline

Two save points!

Level 6 - Make a mistake on purpose, then undo it

  1. In Thonny, delete the whole draw_star function. Save.
  2. Run it: it crashes. Oh no!
git status
git restore hero_badge.py
  1. In Thonny, close the file and open it again (or click into it so Thonny reloads it). The draw_star function is back. Run it - it works.

git restore jumps the file back to your last save point.

Level 7 (boss level) - Make a third commit of your own

Make any change you like (bigger star, new color, add a second star), check it with git diff, then add and commit with a helpful message.

Expected behavior

  • git log --oneline in git-quest shows at least 3 commits.
  • Every message says what changed, e.g. Make star bigger, not stuff or update.
  • git status says nothing to commit, working tree clean at the end.
  • No real name, real email or password appears anywhere.

Checklist

Command cheat sheet

Command What it does Game words
git init start a save system in this folder new save file
git status what changed since the last save? check the pause menu
git add file choose what goes in the next save pack your backpack
git commit -m "msg" make a save point with a label save the game
git log --oneline list all save points, newest first load-game menu
git diff show exactly what changed spot the difference
git restore file throw away unsaved changes reload last save

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read the Level you are stuck on again, and check that Terminal is inside the git-quest folder. Type pwd to see where you are. The command git status also tells you what git is thinking right now.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Git saves in two steps. First you choose what goes in the save, then you make the save point with a label. Use git diff to see what changed before you save. The cheat sheet at the bottom of the README lists every command you need.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: To make a save point, type git add ____ and then git commit -m "____". Put your file name in the first blank and a message that says what changed in the second. To undo unsaved changes, find git restore ____ in the cheat sheet. Put the file name in the blank.
